title: Historical replay and reason-envelope compatibility
risk_being_gated: S4.1 changed the reason attached to every event. The risk is not that new events look wrong - it is that OLD events stop being readable or replayable, which would break the audit chain the whole project depends on.

assertions.full_replay: A/B/R whole streams replay with hash verification ON (replay_events defaults to verify_hashes=True) and reproduce the current state across every REPLAY_FIELDS member
assertions.old_events_unchanged: no historical envelope carries subcode/actor - additive means old events are unchanged, not back-filled
assertions.hashes_intact: every event with a recorded state_hash_after still verifies, and a deliberately corrupted stream is rejected so the check is not vacuous
assertions.reason_always_readable: normalize_reason yields a non-empty code and string subcode/actor for every real event, with no exception on unknown shapes
assertions.r517_lift: the real r517 event still carries final_decision=REOPEN_REVISION_TEXT, its canonical code is the unchanged WORK_REOPENED, and normalize_reason now surfaces REOPEN_REVISION_TEXT as the subcode
assertions.read_only: revision, event count, the sum of payload_json lengths and even the mtime are unchanged after the gate runs - no historical payload may be rewritten
assertions.non_vacuous: the gate asserts the real trees are actually present and each holds >100 events, so it cannot pass by skipping

next_stage: S6 (bounded-advance execution contract + retiring the hand-written driver layer) - the final stage of this goal
note: S4.2 and S4.3 exist in the plan but are outside this goal's objective, which names S4.1; they remain unimplemented and are recorded as such.
